goldens.comment: Using retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1 reads a possibly stale value and can lose increments under concurrency; consider an atomic increment via Prisma (increment: 1) to avoid race conditions (also applies to the similar update in the catch block).

The deletion logic in scheduleSMSReminders.ts incorrectly deletes non-SMS workflow reminders (e.g., Email, WhatsApp) that have retryCount > 1. This occurs because the retryCount condition within the OR clause for deletion lacks a method: WorkflowMethods.SMS filter, causing it to apply to all reminder types instead of only SMS reminders, which is the intended scope of this function.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleSMSReminders.ts:190 — If the retry-count update itself fails or the row was concurrently deleted, the catch block throws and aborts processing every later reminder in the batch.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff, the catch block at line 186-195 adds a prisma.workflowReminder.update call. If this update fails (e.g., row was deleted concurrently, database error), it will throw an exception. Since this is inside a catch block that doesn't have its own try-catch, the exception will propagate up. The code processes reminders in a for loop (visible from the context showing 'for' loop iteration over reminders), so an unhandled exception would abort processing of remaining reminders in the batch. This is a real bug - the retry count update in the catch block should itself be wrapped in a try-catch to prevent cascading failures.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleSMSReminders.ts:159 — A Twilio success followed by a local update failure is counted as retryable and schedules the same SMS again on the next run because the external side effect has no idempotency guard.

adjudication.rationale: The finding identifies a real issue in the diff. Looking at lines 175-186, when scheduledSMS is truthy (Twilio success), the code updates the WorkflowReminder with the referenceId. However, if this prisma.workflowReminder.update() call fails after Twilio has already sent/scheduled the SMS, the catch block at lines 188-196 will increment retryCount. On the next run, since the reminder wasn't marked as scheduled (no referenceId), it will be picked up again and potentially send a duplicate SMS. There's no idempotency key or check to prevent re-sending an already-sent SMS if the database update fails after the Twilio call succeeds.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleSMSReminders.ts:158 — Missing recipients or empty rendered messages bypass both scheduling and retry accounting, leaving permanently unschedulable rows silently pending until their send time passes.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff, when SMS scheduling fails (scheduledSMS is falsy at line 175), the code increments retryCount. However, examining the logic flow, there's a condition check earlier (around line 163-174 based on context) where if recipients are missing or messages are empty, the code would skip both scheduling AND the retry increment in the else block. The deletion logic at lines 31-43 only removes reminders where retryCount > 1 OR scheduledDate has passed. If a reminder has missing recipients/empty messages, it won't be scheduled, won't increment retryCount (staying at 0 or 1), and won't be deleted until its scheduledDate passes. This creates permanently pending rows that silently fail each processing cycle.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleSMSReminders.ts:38 — The unscoped retryCount branch deletes non-SMS workflow reminders once their retry count exceeds one.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows at line 38-42 that the deleteMany query has an OR condition where the second branch only checks `retryCount: { gt: 1 }` without any method filter. This means any WorkflowReminder (not just SMS) with retryCount > 1 will be deleted, including email reminders or other types. This is a real bug where the scope of deletion is broader than intended.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleSMSReminders.ts:190 — If the retry-count update fails, the catch block throws and aborts processing all remaining reminders while masking the original scheduling error.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff, the catch block at line 186-195 adds a prisma.workflowReminder.update call. If this update fails (throws), it would propagate up and potentially abort the loop processing remaining reminders. The original error from scheduling is only logged with console.log, so if the retry-count update throws, the original scheduling error context is lost. This is a real defect - the catch block should handle its own potential failures to ensure all reminders are processed.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/prisma/schema.prisma:1000 — The recurring deleteMany retryCount predicate has no supporting index and can force a full WorkflowReminder table scan as the table grows.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new 'retryCount' column to the WorkflowReminder table and uses it in a deleteMany query with 'retryCount: { gt: 1 }' predicate. The schema.prisma changes show no index is added for retryCount, while other columns like bookingUid and workflowStepId have explicit @@index declarations. This is a valid architectural concern - as the table grows, queries filtering on retryCount without an index could cause performance issues. This is a real, specific concern grounded in the diff, though it's a performance/scalability issue rather than a bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleSMSReminders.ts:190 — If the retry-count update fails, the catch handler throws and aborts processing every remaining reminder instead of containing the per-reminder failure.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff, the catch block at lines 186-195 adds a prisma.workflowReminder.update call to increment retryCount. If this database update fails (throws an exception), the exception will propagate up and abort the entire handler, preventing processing of any remaining reminders in the loop. The catch block doesn't have its own try-catch wrapper, so a failure in the retry-count update would indeed abort processing of all remaining reminders. This is a real defect in error handling logic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleSMSReminders.ts:184 — Retry counts are written from the stale value read by findMany, so overlapping cron invocations can lose increments and keep repeatedly failing reminders alive beyond the intended limit.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows that `reminder.retryCount` is read once via `findMany` at the start, then used later in multiple `update` calls (lines 184 and 193) with `retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1`. If two cron invocations run concurrently, both read the same initial retryCount value, and both increment from that stale value, resulting in lost increments. This is a classic read-modify-write race condition. The deletion logic at line 37 deletes reminders where `retryCount > 1`, so if increments are lost, reminders that should be deleted after 2 failures could persist longer than intended.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleSMSReminders.ts:158 — A reminder with a missing destination or empty message is never scheduled or counted as a failure, so permanently invalid records are retried on every cron run forever.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff, when a reminder has missing destination (sendTo) or empty message, the code at line 158 does `continue` to skip to the next reminder. The new retry logic only increments retryCount when scheduledSMS is falsy (line 178-186) or in the catch block (line 189-196). However, when `continue` is executed due to missing sendTo or empty message, neither the retry count is incremented nor is the reminder deleted/marked as failed. The deletion logic at lines 28-43 only removes reminders where retryCount > 1, so these invalid reminders with retryCount=0 will never be cleaned up and will be retried on every cron run indefinitely.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleSMSReminders.ts:31 — No test exercises cleanup with a non-SMS reminder above the retry limit, leaving the destructive cross-method deletion regression undetected.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows that the deleteMany query at line 31 now uses an OR condition that deletes reminders where EITHER (method is SMS AND scheduledDate is past) OR (retryCount > 1). The second condition has no method filter, meaning it will delete ANY WorkflowReminder (SMS, EMAIL, WHATSAPP, etc.) that has retryCount > 1. This is a real bug - the retry count condition should be scoped to SMS reminders only, but the OR structure means non-SMS reminders with high retry counts will be incorrectly deleted.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleSMSReminders.ts:178 — No endpoint test covers false and thrown scheduling results through successive runs, so retry increments and deletion at the intended threshold are unverified.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces new retry logic with retryCount increments (lines 178-185, 189-196) and deletion of reminders where retryCount > 1 (lines 37-40). This is non-trivial business logic that determines when SMS reminders are retried vs permanently deleted. The finding correctly identifies that there are no tests visible in this diff to verify: 1) retry count increments on scheduling failures, 2) deletion threshold behavior at retryCount > 1. This is a legitimate concern about missing test coverage for newly added logic, not a hallucination.
